opportunities.title: Fix the front door: claim the Google profile, repair the tap-to-call links and add a real quote/booking path
opportunities.problem: The business is hard to find correctly and hard to contact. Its Google Business Profile is unclaimed with no hours and no website link, its Nextdoor page is also unclaimed, and on the site two of the three call buttons dial mistyped numbers (a 9-digit tel:732577013 and tel:7323577013) while the hero phone number is not a link at all. There is no form, booking widget or quote request anywhere, /contact 404s, and hours exist only on third-party listings. Every one of these is a customer-visible failure that happens before any agent could help.
evidence: Google Maps listing displays 'Claim this business', 'Add hours' and 'Add website' at 4.2 stars / 28 reviews - profile unclaimed, no hours, no site link (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Yuhas+Plumbing+%26+Heating+33+Jackson+St+South+River+NJ)

Home page has zero <form> elements; the mid-page CTA links to tel:732577013 (9 digits) and the lower CTA to tel:7323577013 (transposed digits), while the hero number is unlinked text (https://www.yuhasplumbing.com/home)
Site is three pages total - home, plumbing-services, private-policy - with /contact and /about both returning 404 (https://www.yuhasplumbing.com/sitemap.xml)
Triage agent-readiness scores: findable 1, answerable 2, bookable 1, with no hours and reviews locked in images (triage.json, built from https://www.yuhasplumbing.com/home)
Nextdoor page unclaimed ('Is this your business? Claim page') despite Neighborhood Favorite awards 2022-2024 (https://nextdoor.com/pages/yuhas-plumbing-heating-south-river-nj/)
JSON-LD carries address and telephone but no openingHours, geo, priceRange or aggregateRating (https://www.yuhasplumbing.com/home)

Claiming an existing Google Business Profile and then adding hours and a website link is free and is done through Google's own claim/verification flow (https://support.google.com/business/answer/2911778?hl=en)
opportunities.agent_design: This is a build-and-run front-door package, mostly deterministic with agents on the edges. Workstream 1 (human, day one): claim Google Business Profile and Nextdoor page, set Mon-Fri 9-6 hours, website link, services list, emergency line, and photos from the existing install portfolio. Workstream 2 (engineering): replace the broken tel: links with one correct tap-to-call number, make the hero number tappable, add a persistent mobile call bar, embed the JSON-LD openingHours/geo, and stand up per-service and per-town pages generated from the services and 35-town list already on the site. Workstream 3 (agent): a quote/booking intake agent behind a short form - job type, urgency, town, access notes, photo upload - that classifies emergency vs routine, offers real appointment windows, writes the job into a shared calendar/sheet, and texts the customer a confirmation. A human (owner or dispatcher) approves every booking and every price-bearing reply; the agent only quotes ranges the owner has pre-approved. Workstream 4: review-request agent triggered on job close, replying in the owner's voice, with the owner approving templates and any response to a negative review.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A Squarespace template edit will not fix this: the tel: typos, missing form, absent hours schema, town/service page generation, calendar write-back, SMS confirmation and review triggers live in the page source and in integrations between the site, calendar and phone. It also needs ongoing ownership - profile monitoring, hours changes for holidays, review responses - which an owner who is on a truck will not sustain. Off-the-shelf booking widgets also cannot do emergency-vs-routine triage or route to two different numbers.

impact_estimate.range: No verified dollar range is asserted. Quantified baseline: 2 of 3 tappable call paths currently fail or misdial, 0 forms and 0 booking/quote paths exist, and both major listings (Google, Nextdoor) are unclaimed with no hours or site link. Deliverable state: 1 correct tap-to-call path on every page, 1 working quote/booking path, 1 claimed profile with hours and site link, and per-service/per-town pages.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Impact is stated in fixed front-door defects rather than revenue because no call volume, lead count or average ticket is published by any source. Inference, flagged: every mobile visitor who taps the two broken buttons today reaches a dead or wrong number, and every visitor outside 9-6 weekdays (hours per Nextdoor/Birdeye) has no self-serve way to leave a job request. Dollar value cannot be sized without the owner's call log; the pilot should instrument it (call tracking number, form submissions) so month two can be priced from real data.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Weeks 1-2: claim and complete Google Business Profile and Nextdoor (hours, site link, services, emergency number, photos), ship the tel: fixes and mobile call bar, publish openingHours/geo schema, launch a 4-field quote/booking form with emergency routing to (908) 482-8296. Weeks 3-4: 6-10 per-service and top-town pages generated from the existing services and town list, review-request flow live with owner-approved templates, and a before/after snapshot (profile completeness, form submissions, tap-to-call clicks, review count) to size the loss with real numbers.

opportunities.title: After-hours and overflow intake agent that triages emergencies and books routine work
opportunities.problem: All demand arrives through one phone line and one consumer Gmail inbox, during weekday 9-6 hours only, for a crew that is by definition on site or in a basement. Emergency work is sold at an additional cost through a separate (908) number but has no published triage, response commitment or after-hours booking route, so the highest-margin calls are also the ones most likely to hit voicemail.
evidence: No chat, form, booking or quote tool on any of the three site pages; contact routes are tel:7322577013 and mailto:YuhasPlumbers@gmail.com only (https://www.yuhasplumbing.com/home)
Dedicated emergency line (908) 482-8296 with urgent work billed at additional cost, no published after-hours process (https://www.yuhasplumbing.com/plumbing-services)
Hours appear only on third-party listings - Mon-Fri 9:00-6:00, closed Saturday and Sunday (https://reviews.birdeye.com/yuhas-plumbing-heating-166609342213442)

Reviews show responsiveness is the differentiator customers already value (arrival within ~15 minutes of a basement drain-leak call), so a missed call is a lost differentiator, not just a lost message (https://www.bestprosintown.com/nj/south-river/yuhas-plumbing-and-heating-/)

O*NET lists 'discussing system malfunctions with customers to isolate the problem before a truck rolls' and 'scheduling work with customers and initiating work orders' as core tasks for HVAC mechanics/installers (https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/49-9021.00)

NBER working paper (not peer-reviewed as a working paper; cited in the industry brief as the QJE 2025 study): a generative-AI support assistant raised issues resolved per hour by 14% across 5,179 agents, with a 34% gain for novice agents (https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161)
opportunities.agent_design: A voice/SMS agent sits in front of the existing numbers with no change to how customers call. Trigger: inbound call unanswered for N rings, after-hours call, or a web form/SMS lead. The agent asks a short, fixed triage script (water where, is it actively leaking, heat or hot water out, address/town, access), classifies emergency vs same-day vs routine against the owner's rules, and: for emergencies, offers the emergency line handoff and on-call text to the owner with a structured summary; for routine, offers three real appointment windows from a shared calendar and books. It writes one job record (name, town, symptom, photos/voicemail transcript, priority) into a sheet or lightweight FSM, and texts the customer a confirmation with the correct callback number. Human approval points: owner confirms every emergency dispatch and every job over a dollar threshold; the agent never quotes a firm price, only 'diagnostic visit' ranges the owner has set. Recording is off by default, and any transcript retention follows a written policy because calls contain home addresses and access instructions.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A chatbot subscription cannot answer the phone, cannot tell a burst pipe from a dripping faucet, cannot write to a calendar the owner actually uses, and has no escalation path to an on-call tech at 11pm. The hard parts are telephony (porting or forwarding two numbers without breaking the emergency line), the triage decision rules, the after-hours on-call rota, and a reliable job record - all integration and reliability work, not prompt work. Customer data (home addresses, access codes) also argues against a consumer-grade bot.

impact_estimate.range: Avoids or defers roughly 0.25-0.5 FTE of phone/dispatch coverage, worth about $14,000-$27,000 per year in labor capacity, plus an unquantified recovery of currently missed after-hours calls.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Benchmark: NJ dispatcher (SOC 43-5032) annual median $54,590 (May 2025 OEWS), i.e. about $26/hour unloaded; 20 hrs/week of coverage x 52 weeks x $26 = ~$27k at the top of the range, half that at the bottom. This is a labor-substitution estimate for a role the business does not currently staff, so it is capacity avoided, not cash saved today. The 14% throughput figure from the NBER working paper is from customer-support desks (5,179 agents), not contractors - transferring it to a small plumbing shop is an inference and is deliberately excluded from the dollar range. Call volume, emergency mix and average ticket are not published anywhere, so recovered revenue is left unquantified.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks: forward one number (after-hours only at first, to protect the live line) to the agent, build the triage script with the owner from his own 10 most common calls, connect it to a shared calendar and an on-call SMS rota, run 30-60 real calls with 100% human review of transcripts, and report booked-job count, emergency escalations, average answer time and every call the agent could not handle. Go/no-go on whether to put it in front of the main line.

opportunities.title: Quote-to-cash agent: estimate follow-up, job records and invoice/collections chase
opportunities.problem: Nothing in the public footprint suggests a CRM, dispatch, estimating or invoicing system - the shop runs on a phone, a Gmail inbox and paper. That shows up in the reviews as communication friction: one reviewer describes a reasonable repair estimate that was cancelled after they asked a question about it. Jobs that need financing (the site offers it, implying larger installs) are exactly the ones where slow, undocumented follow-up loses the sale, and technicians lose billable hours writing up notes and chasing payment.
evidence: No CRM, dispatch, scheduling, invoicing, review-request, chat or payment tooling visible on any public page; the business email is a consumer Gmail account (https://www.yuhasplumbing.com/plumbing-services)
Financing is offered to qualified customers, implying job sizes that need payment plans and paperwork (https://www.yuhasplumbing.com/home)

Google review describes an estimate the customer thought reasonable but the work was cancelled after a question about it, with the complaint aimed at how the question was handled (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Yuhas+Plumbing+%26+Heating+33+Jackson+St+South+River+NJ)

O*NET core tasks include estimating time, material and labor costs, recording and reporting time and materials on work orders, and keeping records of repairs (https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/47-2152.00)

Only ~28 reviews after 35+ years and 4.2 stars, with no owner responses visible, on unclaimed profiles - no systematic post-job capture (https://reviews.birdeye.com/yuhas-plumbing-heating-166609342213442)
NJ plumber/pipefitter annual median $78,240 (May 2025 OEWS) - the hourly cost of a licensed tech doing paperwork (https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v1/timeseries/data/OEUS340000000000047215213)
opportunities.agent_design: Three connected agents on one job record. (1) Estimate agent: the tech texts photos and a voice note from the site; the agent drafts a structured estimate (scope, parts, labor hours, options, financing link) into a template the owner has approved, and the owner approves or edits every price before it sends. (2) Follow-up agent: tracks each open estimate, sends a short check-in at day 2 and day 7 in the owner's voice, answers routine questions from the company's own price book and warranty terms, and escalates anything technical or negotiated to the owner - directly addressing the 'cancelled after a question' failure. (3) Close-out agent: on job completion, drafts the invoice from the approved estimate plus actuals, sends it with a payment link, chases at day 7/21/45, and triggers the review request. Human approval: all pricing, all collections escalation and any disputed invoice. Records are editable and attributed to the tech for warranty and insurance purposes; no refrigerant or permit records are auto-generated without licensed sign-off.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is a workflow across estimating, invoicing, payments and the phone, with money attached - a chatbot cannot hold a job record, cannot produce an auditable estimate, and cannot be trusted to chase an invoice. It needs a schema, an approval trail, payment integration and consistency between what was quoted, what was done and what was billed. Getting it wrong creates billing disputes and warranty gaps, which is precisely the risk in a licensed trade.

impact_estimate.range: About $3,000-$9,000 per year of licensed-technician time returned to billable work, plus an unquantified share of the open estimates that currently go cold.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Benchmark: NJ plumber median $78,240/yr (May 2025 OEWS) is about $37.60/hour; assuming the agent removes 1.5-4.5 hours per week of write-up, follow-up and invoice chasing (a range, not measured for this shop) gives roughly $2.9k-$8.8k/yr. Assumes the tech currently does this admin himself, which is an inference from the absence of any office/CRM tooling and from O*NET's task mix. Estimate-conversion lift is excluded because no baseline estimate count or close rate is published.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks: instrument one job type (water heater replacement or boiler service) end to end - photo/voice-note intake, drafted estimate with owner approval, day-2 and day-7 follow-ups, invoice and one reminder - measured against the prior month on hours of admin per job, days from estimate to decision, and days from completion to payment. Ship only the estimate-drafting and follow-up pieces if invoicing integration proves too slow.

lead_score.rationale: Pain 27/30: the front-door defects are directly verified, not inferred - two of three call buttons dial wrong numbers, the hero number is unlinked, there is no form or booking path, /contact 404s, and both Google and Nextdoor are unclaimed with no hours or site link. Contact gaps at this level are rare and are visible to every mobile visitor today. Fit 18/20: the top opportunity is exactly capability G with an A agent layered on, and the shop's intake/estimate/invoice gap maps cleanly onto A and D; the only reason it is not 20 is that back-office systems are unknown, so integration scope needs discovery. Ability to pay 13/20: 35+ years trading, Carrier Factory Authorized Dealer, installs plus financed jobs and premium emergency work imply real revenue, but headcount, fleet and revenue are unpublished and the digital footprint (Gmail contact, no CRM, no analytics) suggests a very small owner-operated shop with a conservative spend ceiling. Ease 13/15: claiming the profile and fixing tel: links is days, and a single-site, single-decision-maker business is fast to pilot; minus points because there is no named owner and no schema/systems to plug into. Strategic 14/15: the front-door-plus-intake play is nearly identical for every small NJ plumbing/HVAC contractor, so the assets (profile checklist, tel:/schema fixes, triage script, quote-to-cash templates) re-sell across the ~35-town service area and the wider county. E opportunity deliberately excluded: no avenues.json was supplied in this folder, and the profile shows no camera- or sensor-relevant operation - one office address, no yard, warehouse, kitchen or inventory signals, and the physical evidence is excavation and boiler installs, which are field work, not monitored premises. If the owner wants capability E explored, the only defensible angle would be asset/tool tracking at 33 Jackson St, which cannot be pitched without a site visit.

best_evidence_signal: Two of the three call buttons on the home page dial wrong numbers (tel:732577013 and tel:7323577013) and the hero number is not tappable, while the Google profile is unclaimed with no hours or website link - https://www.yuhasplumbing.com/home
suggested_channel: walk-in - single owner-operated shop at 33 Jackson St, South River; no named owner and a Gmail-only inbox make a doorstep conversation with a printed one-page audit (broken tel: links + unclaimed Google profile) far stronger than email. Bring the audit and ask for two minutes; do not submit anything through the site.
